category_description: How income tax, GST and payroll contributions work in Canada.
subcategory_description: Contributions and premiums that come out of pay.
label: CPP contribution rate for employees and employers
context: Paid by the employee and matched by the employer on pensionable earnings between the basic exemption and the maximum.

label: CPP basic exemption amount
context: The annual amount on which CPP contributions are not required.

label: Maximum annual pensionable earnings (first ceiling)
context: Earnings up to this amount are pensionable for CPP contributions. Above it the CPP2 contribution applies.

label: Most an employee pays in CPP contributions in the year
context: The employer pays the same amount.

label: Most a self-employed person pays in CPP contributions in the year
CPP2 contribution rate for employees and employers
context: Paid on earnings between the first ceiling and the second ceiling.

label: Additional maximum annual pensionable earnings (second ceiling)
context: The upper limit of the earnings on which CPP2 contributions are paid.

label: Most an employee pays in CPP2 contributions in the year
context: The employer pays the same amount.

label: Most a self-employed person pays in CPP2 contributions in the year

subject_intro: The CPP contribution rate and limits for employees, employers and the self-employed, the second additional contribution (CPP2) above the first ceiling, and where Quebec differs.
subject_meta_description: Employees and employers each pay {fact:ca_cpp_rate} CPP on earnings up to {fact:ca_cpp_ympe}. CPP2 applies above that. See the limits and how Quebec differs.
